ref_atoms.ref_content: Verify the countermeasure(s) LC_ESCALATE_EN.INTERSIG.MUBI. Upon randomly switching the life cycle escalation input signal, it is ensured that the DUT stops processing data, locks up and triggers a fatal alert.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Points to the specific life cycle escalation input signal and defines clear expected behavior (stops processing, locks up, fatal alert) upon random switching.

ref_atoms.ref_content: Verify the countermeasure(s) MAIN.CONFIG.SPARSE. Illegally encoded values are written into the main control register via register interface and it is ensured that the values are resolved to the correct legal values. Internal wires carrying the corresponding signals are forced to invalid values and depending on the target wire it is ensured that the DUT stops processing data and signals an alert.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Names the main control register and internal wires, and gives explicit behaviors: illegal writes are resolved to legal values; forcing invalid encodings causes DUT to stop and alert.

ref_atoms.ref_content: Verify the countermeasure(s) AUX.CONFIG.REGWEN. It is ensured that once the REGWEN bit is set to 0, the content of the CTRL_AUX_SHADOWED register cannot be altered anymore until reset.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Specific register (CTRL_AUX_SHADOWED) and bit (REGWEN) with precise write‑locking behavior until reset.

ref_atoms.ref_content: Verify the countermeasure(s) KEY.SW_UNREADABLE. It is ensured that the initial key registers cannot be read via register interface.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Names the initial key registers and explicitly states they are unreadable via the register interface.

ref_atoms.ref_content: Verify the countermeasure(s) DATA_REG.SW_UNREADABLE. It is ensured that the input data registers cannot be read via register interface.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Names the input data registers and explicitly states they are unreadable via the register interface.

ref_atoms.ref_content: Verify the countermeasure(s) KEY.SEC_WIPE. It is ensured that after triggering the clearing of the initial key registers with pseudo-random data, the content of these registers indeed changes to a different value.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Describes a clear-on-wipe mechanism for initial key registers with pseudorandom data and verifiable outcome (value changes).

ref_atoms.ref_content: Verify the countermeasure(s) IV.CONFIG.SEC_WIPE. It is ensured that after triggering the clearing of the IV registers with pseudo-random data, the values read back from these registers via register interface indeed change.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Specific IV registers; describes a wipe with pseudorandom data and checkable outcome (read-back values change).

ref_atoms.ref_content: Verify the countermeasure(s) DATA_REG.SEC_WIPE. It is ensured that after triggering the clearing of the input and output data registers with pseudo-random data, the values read back from output data registers via register interface indeed change and that the content of the input data registers changes to a different value.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Names input and output data registers; defines a wipe with pseudorandom data and verifiable outcomes for both.

ref_atoms.ref_content: Verify the countermeasure(s) DATA_REG.KEY.SCA. SVAs inside aes_cipher_core.sv check that the internal state register gets cleared with pseudo-random data at the end of the last round of every encryption.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Refers to the internal state register in aes_cipher_core.sv and specifies a clear-with-pseudorandom-data behavior at the last round.

ref_atoms.ref_content: Verify the countermeasure(s) MAIN.FSM.SPARSE. It is ensured that upon randomly forcing bits in the state register of the main FSM, the DUT stops processing data, locks up and triggers a fatal alert.
ref_atoms.kind_reason: Names the state register of the main FSM and specifies the exact resulting behavior (stop, lock, fatal alert) upon random bit flips.

ref_atoms.ref_content: Verify the countermeasure(s) MAIN.FSM.REDUN. ref_atoms.kind_reason: Names the redundant logic rails of the main FSM and defines the behavior (stop, lock, alert) when forcing valid/invalid encodings.
